title: The association between in utero exposure to maternal psychological stress and female reproductive function in adolescence: A prospective cohort study.
ehr_evidence: The Raine Study, formed from a pregnancy cohort study, was designed to measure the relationships between early life events and subsequent health and behavior.
summary: Prospective cohort study examining the association between maternal psychological stress (stressful life events) during pregnancy and reproductive function in female offspring aged 14–16 years.
key_findings: Exposure to one or more maternal stressful life events in late gestation was associated with greater uterine volume (β = 0.13, 95% CI 0.04; 0.23) and higher ovarian AFC (β = 0.19, 95% CI 0.02; 0.35) in adjusted multivariate linear regression analyses.
No associations between stressful life events in early or late gestation and circulating AMH or Inhibin B were observed.
captured_features: offspring age, height, BMI, menarche timing
population: 228 female adolescents (aged 14–16 years) from The Raine Study pregnancy cohort in Western Australia
exposure_domain: maternal psychological stress / stressful life events during pregnancy
limitations: moderate sample size limiting statistical power
potential residual confounding by unmeasured pre- and postnatal factors
self-reported stress via questionnaire may vary in perceived severity
transabdominal ultrasound may be less accurate than transvaginal ultrasound
multiple testing without strict Bonferroni correction may increase false positive risk
